summary_requirements: Indexing footprint: ~150M documents (mixed-length PDFs, filings, transcripts). Targets: median embedding kNN latency <= 80ms (eu-west), end-to-end top-10 reranked response <= 200ms for web traffic. Throughput: 300 QPS peak, sustained 120 QPS. Cost sensitivity: target combined cost < $0.02/query at 95th percentile load. Must support canary + A/B rollouts, automatic fallback to baseline embedding set, per-route audit logging, and BYOK for KMS.
migration_plan: Phase 0: holdout & evals - 5k labeled queries, MRR + NDCG baselines
Phase 1: offline embedding comparison (ANN recall) + embedding quantization tests
Phase 2: deploy candidate embedding index in Dedicated private VPC for shadow traffic
Phase 3: cross-encoder reranker canary (1% -> 5% -> 20%) with automated rollback triggers
Phase 4: full switch with A/B experiment and user-level quality monitoring; schedule periodic re-evals
risk_and_mitigation: Quality regression: automated eval thresholds + manual spot checks before ramp
Latency spikes: pre-provision dedicated capacity + smart routing to fallback smaller models
Cost overrun: Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching & caching) and prefix/KV caching
Legal/data residency: isolate regulated corpora to EU-only private nodes; BYOK KMS and audit logs
evals_details: Evals harness: seeded 5k holdout queries representing compliance, audit, and support intents. Metrics: MRR@5, NDCG@10, precision@1, query-level latency, human-graded pass/fail for 300 QA prompts. Comparing current embedding+FAISS baseline vs two candidate embeddings (open-quantized L2 & mixed-precision dot-product) and three reranker checkpoints. Deployment gate: MRR uplift >= 3% OR no more than 1% decrease with manual triage and remediation plan.
pricing_objections: Primary concern: cross-encoder reranker compute (real-time scoring) will increase OPEX. Requested sample cost model for 300 QPS with caching/batching; want uplift justification via reduced support tickets and improved compliance recall. Also request SOW to include pilot compute spend cap.
